steps.text:
Materials Needed: Colored tiles, three each of five different colors.

Overview: This is the final lesson of Level 1. You will be creating real words in three ways to give the student significant practice blending sounds. They will learn that changing a single sound creates an entirely different word, and they will learn the mechanics of rhyming.

sections.title: A: Blend 2 and 3 Sounds into Real Words

steps.text: Last time, you broke words into sounds. This time, we're going to do the opposite. I'll give you some sounds. You'll blend them together to create a real word. Let me show you what I mean.
Tutor touches each tile while saying: "This tile says /a/, this tile says /t/."
Now you touch-and-say those sounds.
Expected: Student touches the first tile while saying /a/, then touches the second tile while saying /t/.
Slowly blend them together.
Expected: /aaaaa/-/t/
Say it fast like a word.
Expected: AT
Perfect. And notice that's a real word. Go ahead and wash off those tiles.

Dictate the remaining sounds in the column: /u/ /v/ (OF), /i/ /t/ (IT), /u/ /p/ (UP), /i/ /ch/ (ITCH), /e/ /j/ (EDGE), /a/ /z/ (AS), /m/ /o/ /p/ (MOP), /th/ /i/ /n/ (THIN), /h/ /a/ /m/ (HAM), /k/ /a/ /sh/ (CASH), /sh/ /e/ /d/ (SHED).
This time, after I give you the sounds and you've come up with the word, we'll do something a little different. But we'll start the same way. Ready?
Expected: Yes
Here are the sounds: /m/ /e/ /t/. Touch-and-say.
Student touches the first tile and says /m/, touches the second tile and says /e/, then touches the third tile and says /t/.
Slowly blend.
Expected: /mmmm/-/eeee/-/t/
Fast like a word.
Expected: MET
Good. Now I'm going to change one of these sounds. Watch carefully. I'm going to change this sound to /p/.
Touch-and-say.
Student touches the first tile and says /p/, touches the second tile and says /e/, then touches the third tile and says /t/.
Slowly blend.
Expected: /p/-/eeee/-/t/
Fast like a word.
Expected: PET
Continue to change one tile at a time to form the following sequence: PEN -> PAN -> FAN -> TAN -> TEN -> TENT (add a 4th tile for /t/) -> SENT -> SEND -> SAND.
Now you're ready for the last step in this book - the last step before we start using letters. You might already know how to rhyme words. But if not, I want to teach you how to rhyme.
Here are the sounds: /k/ /a/ /t/. What is the word?
Expected: Student touches, blends, and says CAT.
Now let me show you with tiles how you can tell if a word rhymes with cat. Rhyming means you change just the first sound.
That sound is /m/. What does that word say now?
Expected: MAT
Right. So CAT and MAT rhyme because only the first sound changed. The rest of the word was the same. So if that says mat, which tile would you change to create a word that rhymes?
Expected: The first one.
Go ahead and change it to a different sound. What does it say?
Expected: Student changes the first tile and says the new word.
Create another one.
Praise the student each time they create a rhyming word, then remove that first tile and encourage them to make another one. Expect: RAT, SAT, FAT, BAT, HAT, NAT, PAT, CHAT.
Tutor returns tiles to the pile and dictates: CHOP
Let's try that once more with a different word. The word is CHOP. Repeat that word.
Expected: CHOP. Student brings down 3 tiles and touches-and-says /ch/ /o/ /p/.
Which tile will you change to create a word that rhymes?
Expected: The first one.
Go ahead and see how many rhyming words you can create.

Expect TOP, SHOP, POP, BOP, COP, HOP, MOP, etc.

CONGRATULATIONS! The student has completed Level 1 and has sufficient Phonemic Awareness skills to begin learning letters in Level 2!
